first_impression.reaction: Our daughter sent this because Mauritius is on her list, and Geoff's first question will be 'is it legal?'. The first lines answer it straight away, 'It will.', which I liked. I read all of it on the iPad. It's calm, careful and leans on government pages, and it's honest about cyclones and insurance, which I didn't expect. But it hands the children a lot of 'ask the Civil Status Office' homework in a country where I don't know who picks up the phone, and it says nothing about deposits, contracts or getting my mother to a beach ceremony.

journey.quote: Mauritius is on the shortlist, and before you fall for a lagoon you want to know one thing: will the marriage count? It will.
journey.reaction: That's exactly the question. Answered in two words. I can forward this paragraph to Geoff as it is.

journey.section: Can Australians marry legally in Mauritius?
journey.quote: Read it once, together, before you sign anything with a resort.
journey.reaction: Good. Someone is telling them to slow down before signing. That's what I'd say.

journey.section: Before you go: entry and documents
journey.quote: The Australian High Commission in Mauritius offers passport, consular and notarial services by appointment only, requested by email.
journey.reaction: So there is an Australian office there, but appointment only, by email. That's not who I ring at 2am if something goes wrong. It makes me want to know even more who would be.

journey.section: What the Civil Status Division asks for
journey.quote: The 3-month window is the detail that catches couples out.
journey.reaction: Very useful. Exactly the kind of thing that goes wrong and costs money. I'll make sure she knows.

journey.quote: It is an application for a certificate, issued under the authority of the Prime Minister, for the publication of a civil marriage between two non-citizens or non-residents.
journey.reaction: I read that twice. Civil Status Division, Central Civil Status Office, Civil Status Office, a Certificate of Authority, a publication. I'm not sure how many offices there are or which one they post things to.

journey.quote: Ask the Civil Status Office which days and hours to come in, and how many working days to allow between landing and the ceremony, then book your flights around the answer.
journey.reaction: Practical, but this is the third or fourth 'ask the Office'. Who actually asks? The children, by email, to a government office overseas? That's where I'd want someone accountable doing it for them.

journey.section: Who performs the ceremony, and where
journey.quote: A fee applies for a wedding in a hotel or other premises, and it is paid at the Central Civil Status Office.
journey.reaction: How much, and in what currency? It's a small thing, but I like to know what we are paying and to whom.

journey.quote: Ask the Office, too, whether the Officer will ask you to choose a matrimonial regime (the legal arrangement for property within the marriage) and which options apply to two non-citizens.
journey.reaction: Property arrangements chosen on a beach in another country? That's the sort of thing Geoff will want a lawyer to look at. Glad it's mentioned, but it worried me and the page leaves it there.

journey.quote: Copies are not accepted unless certified by a notary and the Supreme Court, and acceptance rests with the Apostille Office.
journey.reaction: Heavy going. I gather: keep the original, and allow a spare day. The next paragraph says that more plainly.

journey.quote: Many couples do exactly that: a long lunch at home for the grandparents and friends who could not make the flight.
journey.reaction: A lovely idea, and I'll keep it in mind. But I'd rather know how to get the grandparents there in the first place.

journey.quote: During a cyclone the airport may close and flights may be cancelled or delayed, so check that your travel insurance covers it.
journey.reaction: Honest, and the insurance mention is what I was looking for. Telling every guest to check their own cover and build in a spare day is sensible.

journey.quote: Insect-borne diseases occur in Mauritius, particularly in the warmer months from October to May, and there have been cases of dengue and chikungunya.
journey.reaction: Dengue. My mother is 88. 'Put repellent out' is fine for the young ones, but I'd want to know whether older guests should see their GP first, and which months are safer.

journey.section: Ceremonies on the beach or at your resort
journey.reaction: Yes. That's the sentence I'd underline. The question list before it is good, though none of them asks whether Mum can get to the ceremony spot without stairs or sand.

journey.quote: A Wedded Advisor plans your venue, travel, vendors and payments as one point of contact from start to finish, and confirms inclusions in writing before you commit.
journey.reaction: One person, payments included, in writing. That's what I want when it's our money.

journey.section: Plan your Mauritius wedding with a Wedded Advisor
journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor works in your time zone, quotes in AUD, and agrees the fee in writing before any work begins.
journey.reaction: AUD and the fee in writing. Good. But our time zone is Melbourne and the wedding is six or seven hours behind. Who looks after things on the day there?

unanswered_questions: Who do the couple (or I) ring if something goes wrong in Mauritius outside Melbourne business hours? Is there anyone on the ground on the day? (deferred business detail)
Are our deposits protected if a Mauritius resort or supplier, or Wedded Wonderland itself, fails? Whose name are the contracts in, what language (English or French) and what currency?
Will Wedded Wonderland handle the Civil Status Office correspondence, document posting and the Port Louis appointment, or is that all on the couple? (deferred business detail)
How much is the Civil Status Office fee for a hotel or resort ceremony, and is it paid in rupees on the day?
Should older guests see a doctor before travelling (dengue, chikungunya, the long flight), and which months are kindest for elderly relatives?
Can step-free access to the ceremony spot be checked before booking, for a guest with a walking frame, and is a lawn or terrace safer than sand?
Will Wedded Wonderland arrange transfers from the airport to the resort and to Port Louis, including for a guest with limited mobility? (deferred business detail)
Does the matrimonial regime choice affect anything back in Australia, and should the couple get legal advice before they go?
Is the first conversation a phone call with a real person, and can I join it as a parent paying part?
How is the fee charged, roughly what range, and do you receive commissions from Mauritius resorts? (deferred business detail)
Have you planned real weddings in Mauritius I could look at, and how many? (deferred business detail)
Are there extras or Wedded Privileges for couples who book with you? (deferred business detail)

turn_offs_found.quote: If you offer a wedding package, what exactly does it include for the civil formalities, and what sits outside it?
turn_offs_found.why: My turn-off is pages that skip contracts, deposits and who is responsible. This is the closest the page comes. The word 'deposit' never appears, and nothing says how money paid to an overseas resort is protected or who is accountable if it falls over.

turn_offs_found.quote: It is an application for a certificate, issued under the authority of the Prime Minister, for the publication of a civil marriage between two non-citizens or non-residents.
turn_offs_found.why: Government wording lifted into one long sentence, with several similar office names across the page. I don't mind detail, but I had to reread it on the iPad to work out what it meant for us.

would_share_with: My husband, the intro and 'Getting your certificate ready for Australia', to settle whether the marriage counts at home, plus the matrimonial regime paragraph with 'lawyer?' written next to it
My daughter, the 3-month birth certificate warning and the cyclone and insurance paragraph, so she picks her month carefully and tells the guests about cover

cta_reaction.quote: When you are ready, [start a conversation with Wedded Concierge](https://weddedwonderland.com/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=mauritius-wedding&utm_content=closing).
cta_reaction.why: It's careful and honest, and 'quotes in AUD' and 'fee in writing' are what I want to see. But I'd talk to Geoff first, and I'd only go ahead if it's a phone call with a real person who can tell me how deposits are protected, who deals with the Civil Status Office for the children, who is there on the day, and how they'd get my mother to the ceremony comfortably.

top_3_changes: Add a short practical note for families: older guests seeing a GP before travel given dengue and chikungunya, and adding step-free access to the resort question list, sourced (for example Smartraveller) or flagged for the business; otherwise point to the Advisor for it.

Simplify the office names and the 'application for a certificate, issued under the authority of the Prime Minister' sentence into plain steps (what you post, where, when), and say once which office every 'ask the Office' refers to.

Mention deposits and contracts once in the resort question list (what deposit, refundable or not, which currency, contract in English) and, if sourced, say in the closing that the first step is a phone call and a parent can join.

checks.check: Every journey point and turn-off has an exact quote from the draft
Journey types limited to gained_trust, lost_trust, confused, bored, excited, objection
Stayed in character as Margaret (funding parent): read top to bottom on iPad, focused on deposits, who is responsible, elderly guests, insurance and a phone call
No invented brand facts; on-the-ground support, deposit protection, transfers, paperwork help, fees, commissions, real weddings and Privileges placed in unanswered_questions
VERIFY markers and HTML comments (fact tags, image slots) ignored
Deferred business details listed as unanswered questions, not penalised or made must-fix

open_questions.question: Does the source pack hold anything on health advice for older travellers (dengue, chikungunya, seeing a GP before travel) or the Civil Status Office ceremony fee amount that could support a sentence? If not, flag rather than fill.

assumptions: Margaret arrived via a link from her daughter, reading on an iPad, as a parent contributing about half; relevance is 3 because the page is a legal how-to written to the couple, with little addressed to family or guests.
The wedding time difference reaction ('six or seven hours behind') is Margaret's own rough sense, not a claim taken from the page.
The 3-minute budget covered the full article top to bottom, with the FAQ skimmed as it repeats the body.
